title: Pick the First Non-NULL Name with COALESCE
description:
Users may have a `preferred_name`, a `nickname`, or fall back to their `first_name`. Use `COALESCE` to return the first non-NULL value from those three columns as the display name.

**Table: users** — `id`, `preferred_name`, `nickname`, `first_name`

Return `id` and the resolved display name aliased as `display_name`. Order by `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INT, preferred_name VARCHAR, nickname VARCHAR, first_name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Alicia',NULL,'Alice'),(2,NULL,'Bobby','Robert'),(3,NULL,NULL,'Carol'),(4,'Dave',NULL,'David'),(5,NULL,'Evie','Evelyn'),(6,NULL,NULL,'Frank');
solution_sql: SELECT id, COALESCE(preferred_name, nickname, first_name) AS display_name FROM users ORDER BY id

test_cases.description: 6 rows: Alicia uses preferred_name, Bobby uses nickname, Carol/Frank use first_name, Dave uses preferred_name, Evie uses nickname

hints: COALESCE(a, b, c) returns the first argument that is NOT NULL.
The arguments are evaluated left-to-right; as soon as a non-NULL is found, the rest are skipped.
explanation: COALESCE evaluates its arguments left-to-right: user 1 has preferred_name='Alicia' → 'Alicia'; user 2 has preferred_name=NULL, nickname='Bobby' → 'Bobby'; user 3 has both NULL, first_name='Carol' → 'Carol'; user 4 preferred_name='Dave' → 'Dave'; user 5 nickname='Evie' → 'Evie'; user 6 first_name='Frank' → 'Frank'.
